extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties to PTAB AIA proceedings, USPTO/PTAB stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Interim procedures and solicitation for comment on Director review, Precedential Opinion Panel (POP) review, and PTAB decision circulation/internal review — describing eligibility, timing, composition, scope, and criteria for those processes and inviting stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — eligible requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a party to a case may submit a request for Director review. Third party requests for Director review are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the interim procedure, the USPTO will not charge a fee. The slide also solicits comment on whether only parties should be permitted or whether third-party requests should be allowed (and if so, which ones and why).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — filing procedure to request review
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request Director review of a final written decision in an IPR or PGR by concurrently filing a request for rehearing by the Director of a PTAB decision and submitting a notification of that request by email to Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov, copying counsel for the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the interim procedure implemented June 29, 2021; the web page provides more details and suggestions for parties who wish to request Director review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing by the Director must satisfy the timing requirements of 37 C.F.R. 42.71(d): must be filed within 30 days of the entry of a final written decision or a decision on rehearing by a PTAB panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely request for rehearing by the Director will be considered a request for rehearing under 37 C.F.R. 90.3(b) and will reset the time for appeal or civil action as set forth in that rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — interplay with panel rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: After a panel issues a final written decision, a party may request either Director review or rehearing by the original PTAB panel, but may not request both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party requests panel rehearing and the panel grants rehearing, a party may subsequently request Director review of that decision. If a party requests both Director review and panel rehearing (together or in the alternative), the Office will treat such a request as a request for Director review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — Advisory Committee role and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Director review requests are routed to and considered by an Advisory Committee established by the Director to assist with the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Committee: 11 members; representatives from various USPTO business units; no member may participate in considering a request if that member has a conflict of interest; provides an advisory recommendation to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — decision types and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Director review decisions may be issued as precedential, informative, or routine decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to grant or deny a request: Director review grants will be posted on the Status of Director review requests webpage; denials can be found on the Director review status spreadsheet on the status webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — scope and standard (de novo review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director’s review may address any issue, including issues of fact and issues of law, and will be de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final written decisions by the Director after Director review are appealable to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — conflict/recusal succession
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director has a conflict of interest, she will be recused, and the Deputy Director will take the required action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Deputy Director has a conflict or the position is vacant, the Commissioner for Patents will take the required action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — sua sponte authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate a sua sponte review of a final written decision and may initiate sua sponte review of any PTAB decision, including institution decisions, or a corresponding decision on rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initiated sua sponte by the Director, the parties to the proceeding will be given notice and may be given an opportunity for briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — changes to interim Director review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: Should any changes be made to the interim Director review process, and if so, what changes and why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFC solicits stakeholder input to inform formal rulemaking and any modifications to the interim process pending formalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — who should be permitted to request Director review
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: Should only the parties to a proceeding be permitted to request Director review, or should third-party requests for Director review be allowed, and if so, which ones and why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This solicits views on whether to permit third-party requests and any limits or categories of third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — scope of decisions eligible for Director review
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: Should requests for Director review be limited to final written decisions in IPR and PGR? If not, how should they be expanded and why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This solicits comment on whether to expand Director review beyond final written decisions in inter partes review and post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — criteria to initiate Director review
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: What criteria should be used in determining whether to initiate Director review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFC explicitly asks stakeholders to propose criteria the Office should use to decide when Director-initiated review is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — standard of review to be applied by Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: What standard of review should the Director apply in Director review? Should the standard of review change depending on what type of decision is being reviewed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFC asks whether a uniform standard or different standards based on decision type (e.g., institution vs merits) should apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — standard for sua sponte review of institution decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: What standard should the Director apply in determining whether or not to grant sua sponte Director review of decisions on institution? Should the standard change if the decision on institution addresses discretionary issues instead of, or in addition to, merits issues?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This solicits views on whether institution decisions (including discretionary aspects) should be subject to a different threshold for sua sponte review.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — time limit on reconsidering petition denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: Should there be a time limit on the Director's ability to reconsider a petition denial? And if so, what should that time limit be?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFC asks for suggestions about possible temporal limits on reconsideration of petition denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC question — implications of non-precedential default
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for public comment: Are there considerations the USPTO should take with regard to the fact that decisions made on Director review are not precedential by default, and instead are made and marked precedential only upon designation by the Director?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits input on whether and how the default non-precedential status should affect use and treatment of Director decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — constitutional questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Constitutional questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the standards and procedures used by the POP to decide whether to grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — important statutory/regulatory questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Important questions regarding statutes, rules, regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP considers significance of statutory or regulatory questions when deciding to grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — important issues regarding precedential case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Important issues regarding precedential case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP targets issues that implicate or may affect precedential case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — issues of broad applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Issues of broad applicability to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP looks for issues that will broadly affect Board practice or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — resolve conflicts between Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Resolve conflicts between Board decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP may grant review to harmonize or resolve inconsistent Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — promote certainty and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion used by POP in deciding whether to grant review: Promote certainty and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP review may be used to enhance predictability and uniformity in Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review — default effect, composition, and public input
rubrics_metrics.description: POP review creates binding Board precedent on rehearing by default. POP default composition: Director; Commissioner for Patents; PTAB Chief Judge. An online Amicus Form allows public input on pending POP review requests within seven business days of entry of the Notification of Receipt of POP Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director review process does not alter the current POP process; requests for review of decisions on institution in AIA proceedings or appeal decisions (and other decisions) are accepted for POP review even if not for Director review.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP — purpose and review scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circulation Judge Pool (CJP) provides panels with information on potential conflicts or inconsistencies with relevant authority (including Director-written guidance and other USPTO policy), potential inconsistencies with other PTAB decisions, and suggestions for improved readability and stylistic consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each decision reviewed by the CJP is reviewed by at least two non-panel PTAB judges; the CJP's goal is to provide helpful feedback on decisions prior to issuance and to further consistent, clear, and open decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP — composition and conflict/recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJP is a representative group of at least eight non-management peer PTAB judges; open to any PTAB judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJP members will follow guidance on conflicts of interest set forth in PTAB Standard Operating Procedure 1, notify other CJP members and recuse themselves from any discussion or analysis involving cases on which they are paneled; USPTO follows the Dept. of Commerce's Summary of Ethics Rules in determining conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP — identification of notable draft decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJP identifies notable draft decisions to PTAB Executive Management (e.g., decisions that address issues of first impression, that appear inconsistent with USPTO policy, or that involve areas where policy clarification may be needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB Executive Management may discuss decisions, after issuance, with the Director and/or the Director Review Advisory Committee for consideration for Director-initiated review; and/or the Screening Committee for POP review; periodic meetings may flag areas for potential policy issuance/clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional management review — panel discretion and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any panel member, optionally and at their sole discretion, may consult with one or more members of PTAB management regarding a decision prior to issuance; adoption of any suggestions provided by PTAB management is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless consulted by a panel member, PTAB management does not make suggestions to the panel on any pre-issuance decisions, either directly or indirectly through the CJP. The panel has final authority and responsibility for the content of a decision and determines whether and how to incorporate feedback from PTAB management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-issuance non-involvement of the Director; panel final authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim process makes clear the Director is not involved, pre-issuance, in directing or otherwise influencing panel decisions; the PTAB panel has final authority and responsibility for the content of a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CJP provides a mechanism by which the Director may be made aware of decisions to consider for Director-initiated review or POP review, and of areas to consider for issuing new or modified USPTO policy, but pre-issuance direction from the Director is precluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP eligibility — experience limit for qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the Legal Experience and Advancement Program (LEAP), a patent agent or attorney must have three or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal, including PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAP is designed to aid development of the next generation of patent practitioners and encourage diverse advocates to develop skills before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC procedural comments — how to submit and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform rulemaking, the USPTO published an RFC seeking public input. Comments will be accepted through September 19, 2022, through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links provided to Federal Register and regulations.gov search filter PTO-P-2022-0023 for submitting formal comments.
